SB 1383 SHORT-LIVED CLIMATE POLLUTANT REDUCTION ACT
Senate Bill (SB) 1383 is a statewide effort to reduce emissions of short-lived climate pollutants,
like methane gas. If organic materials (such as paper, cardboard, food scraps, food-soiled paper,
and yard trimmings) are left to decompose in a landfill, the decomposition will emit methane, a
powerful super-pollutant which contributes to climate change.
What does SB 1383
mean for multi-family
properties?
Recycling and organics recycling collection services have
been required for several years in California through
Assembly Bill (AB) 341 and AB 1826. Under statewide
SB 1383 regulations, there are specific and detailed
requirements for all cities, businesses, and residents.
Read this flier to learn about these requirements for
multi-family properties and rental property managers
and owners of multi-family properties.
Mandatory Recycling
In the City of Stockton, properties with 4 or more living units
are considered multi-family properties and are required to
have recycling and organics recycling collection services.

If you have a landscaper that hauls organic waste away from the property, there are specific conditions and
recordkeeping requirements that must be followed. Contact the City of Stockton (209) 937-8831 to ensure you
understand recordkeeping requirements. (Stockton Municipal Code § 8.04.035 and § 8.04.255)
Having a landscaper that hauls green waste to an
organics processing facility does not exempt a
property from required organics recycling service.

Assistance is available
Republic Services and WM have Recycling Coordinators and
Sustainability Advisors available to assist you. The City of
Stockton also has staff available to assist you with educating
your staff, contractors, and tenants. We can assist you with
conducting waste audits and make recommendations for your
multi-family housing property. Do not hesitate to reach out if
you need service or educational tools. We are here to help you
implement a successful recycling program!
